newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban salsa star killed in road accident.
newsitem.headline: Cuban salsa star killed in road accident.

text.p: One of Cuba's best known salsa musicians, Elio Reve Matos, who had developed his own special brand of rhythm known as "charangon", was killed in a road accident, his family said on Thursday.
Reve, who was the director of his own orchestra called Elio Reve y Su Charangon, was 66.

His son Elio Reve Duvergel told reporters the accident occurred on Wednesday night in Matanzas province while Reve was travelling with his orchestra to Villa Clara where they were scheduled to perform in a local carnival.
Reve, who was born in the eastern Cuban city of Guantanamo, was an accomplished percussionist and played the "paila" drums.
He developed his own particular brand of salsa rhythm, the "charangon", a catchy fusion of different musical styles, including "changui" and "son".
Several of Cuba's current salsa stars and musicians, such as Juan Formell, director of the highly popular Los Van Van band, had played at one time or other in Reve's orchestra.
Reve was an officer in Cuba's armed forces reserves and had fought with Cuban forces in Angola in 1975 and 1976. He also held several artistic awards and decorations.
